title: He Won the T20 World Cup Three Months Ago. Now Suryakumar Yadav Is About to Lose the Captaincy.
excerpt: The BCCI has decided to move on from SKY as T20I captain. Shreyas Iyer, Ishan Kishan, and Tilak Varma are in the race to replace him ahead of the Ireland series.
body:
In March, Suryakumar Yadav lifted the T20 World Cup trophy in Barbados. India had defended their title. The captain had delivered the tournament's defining moment of calm — cool eyes, steady hands, a team that believed in him when it mattered most.

Three months later, the BCCI has decided that moment was enough.

According to multiple reports confirmed by The Indian Express, the Board of Control for Cricket in India is set to remove Suryakumar Yadav from the T20I captaincy ahead of India's two-match series against Ireland starting June 26 in Belfast. The decision has already been made. What remains is the formal announcement, expected after a BCCI Apex Committee meeting scheduled for Thursday.

## The Numbers That Changed Everything

The T20 World Cup triumph papered over a decline that the selectors could no longer ignore. In 2024 and early 2025, Suryakumar was the most destructive T20I batter in the world — a 360-degree stroke player who averaged above 40 and struck at nearly 170 in the format.

That player has not shown up consistently since.

In IPL 2026, playing for Mumbai Indians, Suryakumar managed just 270 runs in 13 innings at an average of 20.77. Mumbai finished ninth on the points table. The franchise's campaign was a slow-motion collapse, and the captain's bat was silent through most of it.

His T20I numbers as captain tell a similar story. Since taking over the leadership role, Suryakumar's batting average has dropped to 25.88 — a stark contrast to his pre-captaincy mark of 43.60. Six half-centuries against four single-digit scores is not the ratio the selectors were expecting from their No. 1 batter.

"The selection committee, BCCI and team management, in consultation with coach Gautam Gambhir, have decided that India should go with a new skipper from here on," a top BCCI official told The Indian Express. "Under Surya's captaincy, the team did win the T20 World Cup but keeping his form and future in mind, they felt it's time to move on."

## Who Replaces Him?

The front-runner is Shreyas Iyer. The 31-year-old Mumbai batter has not played a T20I since December 2023. He was not part of India's T20 World Cup squad. On paper, he should be nowhere near the captaincy conversation.

But paper does not account for what Iyer did at the IPL. Captaining Punjab Kings for the second consecutive season, Iyer accumulated 498 runs and led a franchise that has historically underperformed into the playoff conversation. He was already appointed India's ODI vice-captain for the Afghanistan series — a clear signal from the selectors about their long-term thinking.

Iyer's calmness under pressure and his tactical awareness in limited-overs cricket have long been acknowledged. What the selectors see now is a leader who can build a stable core through the 2028 T20 World Cup cycle and beyond, potentially including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will make its debut.

## The Other Contenders

Behind Iyer, two names are generating genuine discussion.

Ishan Kishan, who captained Sunrisers Hyderabad in IPL 2026 after returning from a long exile from the national setup, has impressed with his leadership instincts and aggressive batting. Kishan's three-year absence from international cricket — a period that included a controversial BCCI contract snub — makes his candidacy remarkable, but his recent form and maturity have convinced some within the board that he is ready.

Tilak Varma, at 23, represents the youth option. The left-handed middle-order batter has already shown he belongs at the international level, and his composure in high-pressure IPL matches has not gone unnoticed. If not captain now, Varma is almost certainly being groomed for the role in the future.

Axar Patel's name has also surfaced. The all-rounder served as vice-captain during the T20 World Cup campaign and brings consistency and experience, though he is seen as more of a bridge option than a long-term pick.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian cricket fans in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, this transition carries familiar weight. Captaincy changes in Indian cricket are never just about the cricket. They are cultural events, debated at dinner tables and WhatsApp groups with the same intensity as election results.

The Ireland and England tours — five T20Is and three ODIs across Belfast, Chester-le-Street, Manchester, Nottingham, Bristol, Southampton, Birmingham, Cardiff, and Lord's — will be the first chance for diaspora fans to see the new captain in action. For NRIs in the UK and Ireland, this is cricket arriving at their doorstep during the summer, with a team in the middle of a generational transition.

Suryakumar Yadav may still have a future in the T20I squad as a specialist batter, though even that is not guaranteed. His place in the team now depends on form, not status. The World Cup trophy he held in March bought him goodwill, but the BCCI's patience has a shelf life, and it has expired.

The new captain will be named within days. The new era begins in Belfast.
author: Diaspora Desk
